title: More, most, and just the same
goal: Compare two things with سے, name the "most" with سب سے, and say things are alike — without a word for "than", which Urdu doesn't have.
bekal: comparing two things with … سے … ہے
using سب سے to say "the most"
saying the same, similar, and different

dialogs.title: مکالمہ — لاہور یا کراچی؟
dialogs.intro: In the cafeteria, the talk turns to which city is nicest to live in. Hasan joins in.

lines.speaker: حسن:
lines.text: بودی، آپ کو کون سا شہر زیادہ پسند ہے؟
lines.baca: Būdī, āp ko kaun sā shahar zyāda pasand hai?
lines.id: Budi, which city do you like more?
lines.literal: Budi, you to which city more liked is?

lines.speaker: بودی:
lines.text: لاہور۔ یہ کراچی سے زیادہ خوبصورت ہے۔
lines.baca: Lāhaur. ye Karāchī se zyāda ḵūbsūrat hai.
lines.id: Lahore. It's more beautiful than Karachi.
lines.literal: Lahore. this Karachi from more beautiful is.

lines.speaker: حسن:
lines.text: لیکن کراچی لاہور سے بڑا ہے۔ اور سمندر بھی ہے۔
lines.baca: lekin Karāchī Lāhaur se baṛā hai. aur samundar bhī hai.
lines.id: But Karachi is bigger than Lahore. And it has the sea too.
lines.literal: but Karachi Lahore from big is. and sea also is.

lines.speaker: عائشہ:
lines.text: ہاں، لیکن لاہور میں کھانا سب سے اچھا ہے!
lines.baca: hāñ, lekin Lāhaur meñ khānā sab se achchhā hai!
lines.id: Yes, but Lahore has the best food!
lines.literal: yes, but Lahore in food all from good is!

lines.speaker: بودی:
lines.text: بالکل۔ لاہور کا کھانا پورے پاکستان سے بہتر ہے۔
lines.baca: bilkul. Lāhaur kā khānā pūre Pākistān se behtar hai.
lines.id: Exactly. Lahore's food is better than anywhere in Pakistan.
lines.literal: exactly. Lahore of food whole Pakistan from better is.

lines.speaker: حسن:
lines.text: اور اسلام آباد؟ وہ سب سے صاف شہر ہے۔
lines.baca: aur Islāmābād? vo sab se sāf shahar hai.
lines.id: And Islamabad? It's the cleanest city.
lines.literal: and Islamabad? that all from clean city is.

lines.speaker: عائشہ:
lines.text: صاف تو ہے، لیکن بہت خاموش ہے۔
lines.baca: sāf to hai, lekin bahut ḵāmosh hai.
lines.id: It's clean, sure, but it's far too quiet.
lines.literal: clean indeed is, but very quiet is.

lines.speaker: بودی:
lines.text: جکارتہ لاہور جیسا ہے — بہت رش، بہت زندگی۔
lines.baca: Jakārta Lāhaur jaisā hai — bahut rash, bahut zindagī.
lines.id: Jakarta is like Lahore — very crowded, so full of life.
lines.literal: Jakarta Lahore like is — very crowd, very life.

lines.speaker: حسن:
lines.text: جکارتہ لاہور سے کتنا بڑا ہے؟
lines.baca: Jakārta Lāhaur se kitnā baṛā hai?
lines.id: How much bigger is Jakarta than Lahore?
lines.literal: Jakarta Lahore from how-much big is?

lines.speaker: بودی:
lines.text: تقریباً برابر۔ لیکن جکارتہ زیادہ گرم ہے۔
lines.baca: taqrīban barābar. lekin Jakārta zyāda garam hai.
lines.id: About the same. But Jakarta is hotter.
lines.literal: about equal. but Jakarta more hot is.

lines.speaker: بودی:
lines.text: گرمی کم ہے، لیکن نمی زیادہ۔ اسی لیے برا لگتا ہے۔
lines.baca: garmī kam hai, lekin namī zyāda. isī liye burā lagtā hai.
lines.id: The heat is less, but the humidity is higher. That's why it feels awful.
lines.literal: heat less is, but humidity more. that-very for bad feels is.

notes: **Urdu has no word for "than".** Instead it uses the postposition **سے** attached after the thing being compared: کراچی **سے** بڑا = "bigger than Karachi", literally "from Karachi big". The pattern: **thing compared + سے + adjective + ہے**.

**The adjective itself doesn't change form.** English has *big → bigger*; Urdu doesn't. بڑا stays بڑا, and only سے marks the comparison. If you want to stress it, add **زیادہ** ("more") before the adjective: کراچی سے زیادہ بڑا.

**To say "the most", the thing compared is replaced by سب ("all").** سب سے اچھا = "the best", literally "from all good". The same formula with no exceptions: سب سے بڑا (biggest), سب سے سستا (cheapest), سب سے قریب (closest).

**A few adjectives have their own comparative forms borrowed from Persian.** The comparative of اچھا is بہتر (better) · the comparative of زیادہ is بیشتر (more) · and the comparative of کم is کمتر. These forms are more formal and common in writing; in conversation, سے زیادہ اچھا is just as correct.

**The word جیسا means "like, similar to", and it changes form.** جکارتہ لاہور جیسا ہے (جکارتہ is masculine), یہ کتاب اس کتاب جیسی ہے (feminine). Related: کی طرح ("like", more formal), برابر ("equal, the same size"), ایک جیسا ("exactly the same").

**The word تو in the middle of a sentence means "sure" or "admittedly".** صاف تو ہے، لیکن… = "it's clean, sure, but…". It signals that you partly agree before you push back — much like "sure" or "well" in casual English. It's a little word that instantly makes your Urdu sound natural.

grammars.title: Comparing
body: Three patterns cover every A1-level comparison. Notice that all three use سے, and the only difference is what stands in front of it.

head: Pattern
Example
Meaning
rows: Lahore is more beautiful than Karachi.
یہ اس سے زیادہ مہنگا ہے۔
This is more expensive than that.
یہ اس سے کم مہنگا ہے۔
This is less expensive than that.

after: ⚠️ Notice that the adjective still agrees with **the gender of the noun**, as usual: یہ کتاب اس کتاب سے اچھی ہے (اچھی, because کتاب is feminine). Comparing doesn't free you from the rule of unit 2.

grammars.title: Adjectives often compared
body: This table also reviews adjectives from earlier units, this time together with their opposites and their Persian forms where they exist.
after: Useful intensifiers: بہت (very), تھوڑا (a little), بالکل (completely), تقریباً (about), کافی (quite, fairly), سب سے (most).
To say something is **beyond comparison** — the highest praise — use لاجواب ("unanswerable") or بےمثال ("matchless"): لاہور کا کھانا لاجواب ہے۔

blocks.title: Three Pakistani cities in three sentences
items: Lahore: لاہور پاکستان کا سب سے پرانا بڑا شہر ہے۔ ("Lahore is the oldest big city in Pakistan") — capital of Punjab, city of Mughal gardens, city of food, and the city where you feel Urdu most on the streets.

Karachi: کراچی سب سے بڑا شہر ہے اور سمندر کے کنارے ہے۔ ("Karachi is the biggest city and sits on the sea") — a port city, a business city, and the city with the most languages: Urdu, Sindhi, Pashto, Punjabi, and Gujarati can all be heard on a single street.
Islamabad: اسلام آباد سب سے نیا اور سب سے صاف شہر ہے۔ ("Islamabad is the newest and cleanest city") — built from scratch in the 1960s as the capital: orderly, green, and — as Ayesha says — quiet.
Lahore is more beautiful than Karachi.
This is more expensive than that.
